passage: For three weeks, Pema kept the maths paper folded inside the geography textbook. It had a red 12 out of 50 on top. Every evening in the village house, when Aai Nirmala asked, "How was school?" Pema answered, "Fine," and went to feed the goats. The paper began to feel like a hot coal. At night Pema imagined the shouting, the disappointed silence, worse than shouting. On Sunday, Nirmala found the paper while dusting. She sat down beside Pema and said quietly, "I'm not angry. I'm worried you carried this alone." Pema burst into tears. "I was scared," Pema said. "Then let's look at it together tomorrow," said Nirmala.

qa.q: Where did Pema keep the maths paper?
qa.a: Folded inside the geography textbook.

qa.q: What was Pema afraid of when imagining the response at night?
qa.a: The shouting, and worse, the disappointed silence. Pema's fear of the reaction was what drove the hiding.

qa.q: What did Nirmala do that helped Pema after finding the paper?
qa.a: Nirmala sat down beside Pema, said calmly that she was not angry but worried Pema had carried it alone, and proposed looking at it together.

qa.q: How might Nirmala have felt finding the paper after three weeks of "Fine"?
qa.a: Worried and sad that Pema had hidden it, but caring, since Nirmala responded gently and offered to help.

grounding: A teenager hides a failed test for weeks out of fear of Aai Nirmala's reaction, and the fear rather than the news drives it.

passage: Mina had borrowed the school's laptop for the robotics club. In the second week, it slipped out of the bag on the tram and was gone. Mina said nothing. The next morning Mina told the club leader, "I forgot it at home." Then "I'll bring it Monday." Then Monday came. In Toronto's cold, Mina walked the long way home, rehearsing, and never finishing the sentence. It wasn't the laptop that scared Mina. It was Mama Rania's face. Finally, at dinner, Mina said, "I lost the laptop three weeks ago." Rania set down the spoon. "Thank you for telling me. We will call the school together tomorrow morning."

qa.q: Where did the laptop go missing?
qa.a: It slipped out of the bag on the tram.

qa.q: What was Mina afraid of, according to the passage?
qa.a: Mama Rania's face, more than the laptop itself. Fear of the reaction kept Mina silent for weeks.

qa.q: What did Rania do when Mina finally told?
qa.a: Rania set down the spoon, thanked Mina for telling, and said they would call the school together the next morning.

qa.q: How might the club leader have felt hearing three different excuses?
qa.a: Confused and maybe worried, not knowing what happened, and Mina's changing story left the leader unable to help until the truth came out.

grounding: A teenager conceals a mistake for weeks out of fear of Mama Rania's reaction, and the fear of the response drives concealment.

passage: Kiran had failed the Class 11 maths unit test three weeks ago, and the paper was still folded inside a chemistry book at the bottom of the cupboard. Every evening, when Papa asked, "How are studies?", Kiran said, "Fine." Every evening, the fold in the paper felt heavier. It wasn't the 12 out of 50 that scared Kiran most. It was Papa's face when Kiran's cousin had failed, the way he'd gone silent for days. Kiran couldn't stand that silence. Sarika, Kiran's younger sister, found the paper while looking for her chemistry book. "You failed? Three weeks ago?" Kiran grabbed it. "Don't tell Papa." Sarika looked at Kiran for a long time. "He'll be more upset that you hid it." That night, Kiran put the paper on Papa's desk. Papa read it, then said, "Why didn't you tell me?" Kiran whispered, "I was scared of your silence."

qa.q: What did Kiran score on the maths unit test?
qa.a: 12 out of 50.

qa.q: What was Kiran most afraid of?
qa.a: Kiran was afraid of Papa's silence and disappointment, more than the failed mark itself.

qa.q: What did Sarika say that helped Kiran decide to tell?
qa.a: She said Papa would be more upset about the hiding than the mark.

qa.q: How might Papa feel hearing that Kiran feared his silence?
qa.a: Papa would probably feel sad and surprised, realising his reaction made Kiran hide things.

grounding: Shows a teenager hiding a failed test for weeks out of fear of a parent's reaction rather than the result itself.

passage:
"Gopika, why are you jumpy every time your mum calls?"
"Nothing."
"Come on," said Aditi. "It's been two weeks."
Gopika sighed. "I cracked her phone screen. I dropped it when I was using it for my project. I put it back in the drawer and said nothing."
"She hasn't noticed?"
"She uses her work phone. But she'll notice soon."
"Why not just tell her?"
"Because last time I broke something, she shouted for an hour. I can't do that again."
"So it's not the phone. It's the shouting."
Gopika nodded.
"If she finds it herself, it'll be worse."
"I know." Gopika picked at her nails. "Will you come with me when I tell her?"
"I'll wait outside," Aditi said. "Tell her today, before she finds it."

qa.q: What did Gopika crack?
qa.a: Her mother's phone screen.

qa.q: What was Gopika really afraid of?
qa.a: She was afraid of her mother shouting for an hour, more than of the cracked phone itself.

qa.q: How did Aditi help Gopika decide to tell?
qa.a: She pointed out it was the shouting Gopika feared, and offered to wait outside while Gopika told her mother today.

qa.q: How might Gopika's mother feel if she found the phone herself?
qa.a: She would probably feel angrier and hurt that Gopika hid it for two weeks.

grounding: Shows a teenager hiding a mistake for weeks out of fear of a parent's reaction rather than the mistake itself.

passage:
Last winter I scraped Papa's scooter against the colony gate. A long silver scratch down the side. I parked it with that side to the wall and said nothing.
For five weeks, every time Papa went out, my stomach flipped. My brother Ramesh noticed. "Why do you keep checking the parking?"
It wasn't the scratch I was scared of. It was the way Papa gets when something he loves is damaged. The loud voice, the lecture, the not-talking.
Then one morning Papa found it. He came in holding the keys. I started crying before he said anything.
He was angry, yes. But then he said, "I'm more upset that you hid it for five weeks. I'd rather hear bad news from you."
I'm Aadhya. I think hiding was worse than the scratch.

qa.q: Where did Aadhya scrape the scooter?
qa.a: Against the colony gate.

qa.q: What was Aadhya afraid of during the five weeks?
qa.a: Aadhya was afraid of Papa's loud voice, lecture and silence, not the scratch itself.

qa.q: What would you advise Aadhya for next time?
qa.a: Tell Papa soon, even if scared, since hiding made the worry longer and Papa said he'd rather hear bad news directly.

qa.q: How did Papa feel when he found out?
qa.a: He was angry, but more upset that Aadhya hid it for five weeks.

grounding: Shows a teenager hiding a mistake for weeks out of fear of a parent's reaction, not the news itself.

passage:
Class teacher's note, 12 November.
Payal's mid-term chemistry paper (22 out of 80) was returned on 20 October. The signed copy has still not come back. When I asked today, Payal first said her mother was travelling, then that the paper was lost. Her hands were shaking. After class, with no one around, I asked what she was worried would happen. She said, "Mumma will be so disappointed she'll go quiet for days. That's worse than shouting." I told her the mark can be fixed and that hiding it has only made it heavier. With her permission I called her mother, Sangeeta, this afternoon. She said she had no idea and was sad that Payal felt she couldn't tell her. We meet together on Thursday, with Payal present.

qa.q: What did Payal score in the chemistry paper?
qa.a: She scored 22 out of 80.

qa.q: What was Payal most afraid of?
qa.a: She was afraid of her mother's disappointment and days of silence, which felt worse to her than shouting.

qa.q: What steps by the teacher helped?
qa.a: Asking privately what Payal feared, saying the mark can be fixed, and calling her mother that afternoon, with Payal's permission, to plan a meeting together.

qa.q: How did Sangeeta react to learning about the paper?
qa.a: She said she had no idea and felt sad that Payal thought she couldn't tell her.

grounding: Shows a teenager hiding a failed test for weeks out of fear of her mother's reaction, and a teacher helping bring it into the open.
